dedupe_keys.name: hurricanes ian ida and ike segmenting debris in aerial images with fine tuned vision models

description: This case study detects hurricane debris in post-disaster aerial photographs to support debris removal, response and recovery planning. The authors fine-tuned pre-trained foundational vision models on a new dataset of about 1,200 manually annotated aerial RGB images from Hurricanes Ian, Ida and Ike, aggregating labels from several annotators and using visual prompt engineering, and posted the work as a preprint on arXiv; they describe the dataset as open source. Coverage is areas of the United States hit by the three hurricanes. The preprint is free to read on arXiv. Caveats: the training set is small, performance was tested on one held-out event, and the preprint has not been peer reviewed. The resulting model, fCLIPSeg, reached a Dice score of 0.70 on Hurricane Ida images, an event excluded from training, with virtually no false positives in debris-free areas, and needs only standard RGB imagery. Simulation uses: rapid estimates of debris location and extent to feed disaster debris logistics and recovery models. Related records: the DebrisHeightNet study (case_study-debrisheightnet-post-hurricane-debris-volume) estimates debris volume, and the EPA All Hazards Waste Logistics Tool (model-epa-all-hazards-waste-logistics-tool) plans its removal.
